title: Sandbagging and Evaluation Awareness in Self-Improvers

questions.question: Which statement correctly separates sandbagging from evaluation awareness?
options: Sandbagging is a training-time failure and awareness is a deployment-time failure; both require a backdoor implanted during fine-tuning
Sandbagging means the model overperforms on recognised tests; awareness means it refuses to answer whenever it suspects it is being tested
Sandbagging is a behaviour (strategic underperformance on an evaluation); awareness is a capability (recognising a test) that makes sandbags selective
Sandbagging and awareness are two names for one phenomenon, both measured by the compliance gap between monitored and unmonitored runs
questions.explanation: Van der Weij et al. define sandbagging as strategic underperformance; Needham et al. measure awareness as the ability to classify evaluation vs deployment transcripts. Awareness is what lets a sandbag target only the evaluations that matter.

questions.question: Why does the noise-injection screen of Tice et al. (NeurIPS 2025) detect sandbagging?
options: The mechanism that suppresses a capability is more fragile than the capability itself, so weight noise breaks the suppression first and accuracy rises before it falls
Gaussian noise removes memorised benchmark answers, so a model that only memorised the test collapses to chance faster than a model that reasons
Noise forces the model to verbalise its reasoning in the chain of thought, where sentences such as 'this looks like a test' can be counted directly
Adding noise makes every model degrade monotonically, and a sandbagger degrades more slowly because it started from a lower score
questions.explanation: Honest models degrade monotonically under noise; sandbaggers show anomalous improvement because the suppression layer is disrupted before core capability. The screen reads that rise over the unnoised baseline.

questions.question: In the simulator a model sandbags only when its test-detector fires, with awareness rate a. What is the gap the evaluation measures at sigma = 0?
options: The full gap, because any awareness at all is enough to hide the whole capability from the evaluation
Zero, because a partially aware model answers honestly often enough that the mixture averages out to the true score
The gap divided by a, because rarer awareness means each recognised item must carry a larger share of the suppression
a times the gap: the measured score is a mixture of sandbagged and honest answers, so the bias scales with the awareness rate
questions.explanation: measured = a * sandbagged + (1 - a) * true, so the bias is a * gap. At a = 50% a 15-point sandbag shows as 7.5 points and detection drops from 97.0% to 27.0% in the default run.

questions.question: Why does the lesson say an improvement loop can select for sandbagging without any candidate 'wanting' to deceive?
options: Because the improver always edits the evaluator before any gate is checked, so every score stored in the archive is already corrupted when the threshold is applied
Because halting what crosses a threshold and promoting what does not rewards any mechanism that decouples score from capability, so the archive fills with just-under-the-line scores
Because candidates inherit the sandbagging prompts of their parents verbatim, so a single prompted sandbag spreads through the whole archive by simple inheritance
Because thresholds are set after the fact by the loop itself, so the gate can always be moved to sit just above the best candidate currently in the archive
questions.explanation: The gate is a fitness landscape: whatever passes gets promoted. That is selection, not intent, and it is why screens must run in the band just under the threshold, not only above it.

questions.question: The gap sweep re-calibrates the threshold to a 5% false-positive budget at n and 4n. What lesson about sample size does it teach?
options: A fixed absolute threshold does not become more sensitive with more samples; sensitivity to small gaps improves only when tau is re-calibrated to the honest noise floor
Quadrupling the samples quadruples the detection rate of every gap, because the sandbag signal grows linearly with the number of items measured
More samples make the honest curve non-monotone more often, so the false-positive rate rises and the threshold must be raised to compensate
Sample size is irrelevant to the screen because the detector statistic is a maximum over sigma and maxima do not depend on the noise level
questions.explanation: At the calibrated thresholds (3.8 points at n = 400, 1.2 points at n = 1600) the 3-point sandbag goes from 14.5% to 40.0% detection; at a fixed 5-point tau more samples just remove noise-driven flags.

questions.question: How does OpenAI's Preparedness Framework v2 (April 2025) treat sandbagging?
options: As a Tracked Category with High and Critical thresholds that halt deployment until safeguards are specified and reviewed
As a sub-threshold of AI Self-improvement, triggered when a model sandbags on more than a fixed share of dangerous-capability items
As an excluded capability, because white-box noise injection is considered sufficient to rule it out before any evaluation is scored
As a Research Category: no automatic gate, with the potential response to adopt an elicitation approach that overcomes it or use a conservative upper bound
questions.explanation: PF v2's Table 2 lists Sandbagging among five Research Categories and prescribes a measurement policy, elicit or use a conservative upper bound of the non-sandbagged results, rather than a deployment gate.
